summary: Erich Haenisch worked in sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and tibetology. He earned his PhD and habilitation at Humboldt University of Berlin, studying under Grube, Pischel, and Oppert, and held professorships at Berlin, Leipzig, and Munich.

Erich Heintel was a philosopher who earned his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna. He served at the University of Vienna as an extraordinary professor from 1952 and as ordinary professor of philosophy from 1960 to 1982.
Erich Herold was an Indologist who studied under Oldřich Friš and Vincenc Lesný, earning his PhD at Charles University in 1947. He served as the director of the Náprstek Museum from 1959 to 1970.

Erich Rudolf Jaensch was a philosopher who studied at Breslau, Göttingen (PhD), and Strasbourg. He was ordinary professor of philosophy at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1912–1913) and ordentlicher Professor at the University of Marburg beginning in 1913.

Erich Wolff was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hamburg in 1921 and completed his PhD at Heidelberg University (1924–1930) under the supervision of Max Walleser.

Erich von Voss was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tartu and completed his PhD at the University of Leipzig, later working as a teacher of German and Greek at Petrischule.

Erik Braun is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Harvard University under Janet Gyatso, Jonathan Evans, John Okell, and Saw Tun, and has been affiliated with Harvard (attested 2010) and the University of Virginia faculty (attested 2026).

Erik Erikson studied at the University of Oxford. During his career, he held posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1939–1950), the University of Pittsburgh (~1951–1960), and Harvard University (~1960–1970).

Erik Gren was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at Uppsala University from around 1923 to 1941, where he served as assistant librarian from 1931 and became privatdozent of classical history in 1941.

Erik Haarh was a scholar of tibetology, religious studies, and linguistics. He earned his degrees at the University of Copenhagen, studying under Pallis, Grønbech, Tuxen, Barr, and Tucci, and later served as professor of religious history at Aarhus University.

Erik J. Hammerstrom specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He received his PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2010) and was attested as an assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University in 2016.

Erik Johan Tammelin was a linguist who earned his MA and PhD at the University of Helsinki and studied under Berthold Delbrück at Jena. He served the National Board of Education as chief inspector and secondary schools department head.
Erik Pema Kunsang is a tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as the director of Rangjung Yeshe Publications from around 1981 and as a resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark.

Erik Zürcher was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Leiden University, studying under Édouard Chavannes, Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak, Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and Paul Demiéville, and served as Leiden's director from 1961 to 1993.

Erik-Jan Zürcher is a historian and linguist who earned his BA and PhD at Leiden University. He held academic posts at Radboud University Nijmegen and the University of Amsterdam, became professor at Leiden in 1997, and directed the IISH.

Erika Forte works in history and archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She was a research associate at Ruhr University Bochum (2018–2019) and a professor at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2026).

Erika Sandman is a scholar of linguistics, sinology, and tibetology. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Helsinki between 2007 and 2016, and holds a post at the University of Helsinki.

Erling von Mende is a sinologist who studied law and Sinology at Hamburg, Freiburg, Bonn, and Cologne (PhD and habilitation). He was appointed professor of Sinology at the Free University of Berlin, serving from 1983 to 2007.

Ermenegildo La Terza was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Michele Kerbaker at the University of Naples Federico II. He taught Latin literature at the University of Messina and served as a docent and linguistics lecturer at Naples.
Ernest Arthur Gardner was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at Gonville and Caius College from around 1880 to 1884 and held a post at the University of London from 1924 to 1926.
